aliases: a circle needs more than one chart
purpose: Can a smooth circle need a second coordinate map?
meaning: Compute the unit-circle point from its angle. Project from the north or south pole to the horizontal coordinate line. A chart excludes its chosen pole; the other chart covers that point.

definition.setting: A marker moves around a circular track. To give its position one straight-line coordinate, project a line from a chosen pole through the marker. The coordinate grows large near that pole and is unavailable at the pole itself. Switch the projection pole: the track and marker stay in place while their coordinate changes.
conditions: The unit circle is covered by two stereographic charts. A chosen projection omits its own pole, although the circle is smooth there. Coordinate values are numerical and may leave the displayed window; a chart is not an isometric map.
The displayed calculation, coordinates and marks are evaluated from the same declared input state.
